newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Bosnia denies charges of warcrimes perjury plot.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia denies charges of warcrimes perjury plot.

text.p: Bosnia's Moslem-led government on Saturday denied charges it forced a key prosecution witness to lie at the war crimes trial of Bosnian Serb Dusan Tadic.

"To come to the conclusion without any sort of investigation that somehow the (Bosnian) government is culpable here is extremely...unfair," Bosnia's United Nations representative Mohamed Sacirbey told Dutch television.

U.N. prosecutors on Friday withdrew the testimony of Dragan Opacic, previously known only as witness "L", after a warcrimes investigator testified Opacic had been trained by Sarajevo military police to lie to the court about Tadic.

Opacic appeared before a closed session of the U.N. tribunal in The Hague in August, telling the court he served as a guard at the Serb-run camp of Trnopolje in northwest Bosnia where he saw Tadic commit atrocities.
U.N. investigator Robert Reid told the court on Friday that Opacic, a Serb, had claimed he would be executed by Bosnian authorities unless he falsely testified against Tadic.

Sacirbey said the allegations of Bosnian government involvement were devised to undermine the tribunal and prevent its two most wanted men -- Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and military commander General Ratko Mladic -- from being brought to trial.
"We think frankly that it is intended as a way to avoid the very difficult task of bringing others such as Karadzic and Mladic to justice," he said via a satellite link from New York.
Opacic, convicted by a Bosnian court, had a vested interest in discrediting the Bosnian authorities to avoid serving his sentence, Sacirbey said.
He said the Bosnian government would cooperate fully with a U.N. investigation into the affair.

Tadic, 41, is accused of visiting three camps in northwest Bosnia -- Trnopolje, Omarska and Keraterm -- to kill, torture and rape non-Serbs as part of an "ethnic cleansing" campaign in the region in 1992. He denies the charges.

Prosecutor Grant Niemann said on Friday he was dropping a charge relating to Trnopolje. Tadic still faces a maximum life jail term if found guilty of 30 other counts of committing atrocities at Omarska and Keraterm.
